transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
Well, it's my ankles, doctor. They've both been swelling up, and I'm not sure why.
When did you first notice the swelling in your ankles?
It started about four weeks ago, I think. I just noticed my ankles looking puffy one evening.
Have you ever had any bad reactions or allergies to any medicines?
No, I've never had any trouble with medicines. Nothing that I know of, anyway.
How much, if at all, is the swelling in your ankles affecting your day-to-day life?
Well, my shoes feel tight by teatime, and I've stopped wearing my usual shoes because of it. I've taken to sitting with my feet up in the afternoons.
Can you tell me about any medicines you've taken in the last few weeks?
I take a small water tablet each morning, though I can't remember the name of it. And I'm on a blood pressure tablet — I'm still on the 5 mg one, I think.
Have you ever had any operations?
No, I've never had any operations.
How would you describe the swelling in your ankles — would you say it's mild, moderate, or severe, or you're not sure?
I'd say it's mild, really — it's a bit uncomfortable, maybe a 3 out of 10. It's more that it's bothersome than painful.
Have you noticed anything else going on, apart from the swelling in your ankles?
No, nothing else really. I've not had any chest pain or trouble breathing, if that's what you mean.
Is there anything you've noticed that seems to make the swelling better or worse?
Yes — it's always worse by the evening, and it's mostly gone in the morning after I've been lying flat overnight.
What worries you most about the swelling in your ankles?
I suppose I'm worried it might mean my heart is failing. My sister had heart failure, you see, and it frightens me that this could be the same thing.
Is there anything else about your health in the past that you’d like to tell me?
Yes, I've got high blood pressure, and I've been told my kidney function is a bit reduced. That's about it, really.
Could you tell me the names and doses, if you know them, of any medicines you take regularly or have started or changed recently — is it none, one or two, three or more, or are you not sure?

Well, I take the water tablet in the morning but I can't remember its name. And the blood pressure one — actually, now that I think again, they did increase my amlodipine from 5 mg to 10 mg about six weeks ago. And I take simvastatin 20 mg at night.

I just want to get this right — you mentioned a water tablet each morning and a blood pressure tablet that you're still taking at the 5 mg dose, but also that your amlodipine went up from 5 mg to 10 mg about six weeks ago; which of those is actually the case?
The right one is that my amlodipine was increased to 10 mg about six weeks ago — I misspoke earlier. I got mixed up for a moment.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
